# 2. The Sharing–Sparing Axis {#sec-sharing-sparing}

The axis answers one question: **what happened to agricultural production on this ground?** Every ground-mounted project occupies one of five positions, S1 through S5. The axis is largely independent of [scale](1-the-scale-transect.qmd): scale says what was available; position says what happened.

Many arguments about solar on farmland make an unspoken position claim [@moore2022]. Naming it first clarifies what a project can claim, what it must still argue for, and which objections apply. The framing borrows the neutrality of conservation ecology's land-sharing and land-sparing debate [@green2005; @phalan2011]; it does not rank positions by definition.

### 2.1 The positions {#sec-positions}

::: {.position-table}
| Position | Description | Characteristic |
|---|---|---|
| **S1 — Full sharing** | Production continues within the array footprint, in the same ground | Vegetable [agrivoltaics](5-terminology.qmd#term-agrivoltaics); crops between rows |
| **S2 — Functional sharing** | Ground layer is productive but subordinate to the array; grazing, forage | Solar grazing at any scale |
| **S3 — Coexistence** | *Neither sharing nor sparing.* The array takes ordinary ground outright, production stops on it, and the revenue sustains the farm enterprise that holds it. Land and farm coexist at the level of the business rather than the field | The lease that keeps a working farm solvent and in operation |
| **S4 — Idled-land sparing** | Array occupies ground already idle, marginal, or out of production, so that productive land is spared | Awkward remnants, fallow ground, brightfields |
| **S5 — Impaired-land retirement** | Production ends on ground that carried a measurable off-site burden, such as chronically low yields, high runoff, nutrient or pesticide export, or irrigation draw beyond the aquifer's budget, or on ground positioned where that burden can be intercepted | Prairie strips on runoff-prone ground; retiring drainage-impaired irrigated fields |
:::

Coexistence is the center of the axis and where most projects sit; direct crop production under panels remains a small share of US installations [@stid2022; @macknick2022]. **S3 is where restoration is socioeconomic before it is biophysical**: the lease sustains the farm enterprise although production stops in the footprint. Where rent reaches a non-farming owner and the operation ends, the site is **bare conversion**, the non-restorative baseline. The distinction must be made for the landowner and tenant separately (§4.5) [@stid2025].

S4 and S5 both end production but differ in where benefit lands. S4 moves solar onto ground already idle or marginal, sparing land not taken. S5 retires ground carrying a measurable off-site burden, acting on the ground taken and its downstream effects. Prairie plantings on drainage-impaired crop ground illustrate the distinction [@schulte2017]. Corn-ethanol land offers a large S5 case: solar can deliver comparable energy on a small fraction of the area, but the electricity-for-fuel substitution remains imperfect [@sturchio2025croplands].

A position records the ground fact, not project quality. Pollinator habitat, prairie, and native grassland are [restorative functions](4-restorative-functions.qmd), not positions: the same planting can occur at S2 through S5. The axis says what happened to production; §4 says what the land was made to do.

The positions are exclusive, and two questions in order settle which one applies.

1. **Does agricultural production continue within the footprint?** If it does, the site is **S1** (production in the same ground) or **S2** (a productive but subordinate ground layer), whatever the ground used to be. A flood-prone corner that still carries the farm's sheep is S2, not S4.
2. **If production has stopped, what was the ground beforehand?** Ordinary productive land gives **S3**, ground already idle or marginal gives **S4**, and ground carrying a measurable off-site burden gives **S5**. The same flood-prone corner, left to naturalize under the panels, is S4.

S3 asks one further question: does the farm enterprise survive the conversion? If not, it is bare conversion.

Sparing remains a landscape claim: S4 benefits only if the land left untaken was the genuine alternative and the array did not move onto something else worth keeping [@gallaher2026]. S4 includes unlike sites, from remnants to brownfields, whose contamination and permitting constraints still belong in the site description. Building-mounted arrays are [A0](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-zones) and hold no position.

### 2.2 Which positions scale allows {#sec-wedge}

Scale narrows the positions available through [siting latitude](1-the-scale-transect.qmd#sec-siting-latitude). At A4–A5, contiguous land assembly near a substation makes selective sparing difficult. S4 thins because idle remnants are scattered; S5 can scale where impairment is regional. The *feasible wedge* is widest at A3 and narrows toward S2–S3 at both ends of the transect.

![The feasible region as a lens on a centred five-position axis, widest at A3 (Parcel) and closing toward the S2–S3 middle at both extremes of scale. Grazing (S2) and coexistence (S3) run the spine at every scale. Solid points are exemplar practices; hollow points are exceptions that reopen a thinned corner. Hatching marks where the space thins, lightly at small scale (feasible but atypical or negligible) and densely at large scale (strongly constrained).](../figures/fig_feasible_wedge.svg){#fig-wedge}

Grazing and coexistence form the spine. The thinned corners remain possible: greenhouse photovoltaics at small scale, vertical bifacial arrays for utility-scale S1 [@vaverkova2026], pre-disturbed land for S4, and regional impairment for S5. Native grassland remains a [restorative function](4-restorative-functions.qmd), not a position [@walston2025; @krasner2025].

S1 is climate- and crop-conditional: it is most plausible for shade-tolerant crops in hot, water-limited settings and mixed to negative for staple grains in temperate or humid settings [@barrongafford2019; @weselek2019; @merheb2025].

American Farmland Trust's production-based [dual-use](5-terminology.qmd#term-agrivoltaics) definition requires S1 or S2. Critics include ecovoltaics, whose ecological ground layers sit as functions at S3 and below [@hernandez2019]. This document describes that dispute rather than settling it.

### Terms

Terms introduced in this section are defined in the [Terminology](5-terminology.qmd) chapter (§5), under [Sharing and sparing](5-terminology.qmd#sec-terms-sharing), alongside every other term the document defines.
